db: Arthropods do not possess an exoskeleton composed primarily of peptidoglycan.

In a population with a recessive allele b causing cancer, 1 in 400 people have the disease. In Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the expected proportion of individuals carrying the b allele but not expected to develop cancer is 0.25 or 25%.
The presence of similar structures (homologous structures) between two organisms, such as the humerus in humans and birds, suggests that they share a common ancestor and belong to the same clade.
The pressure-flow model of phloem movement does not rely on an ATP-dependent pressure-flow pump to transport photosynthate from source to sink.
Centromeres contain DNA sequences required for the segregation of chromosomes during both mitosis and meiosis.
The most effective way to control a mosquito population is not to maintain it at the midpoint of its logistic curve, which is a common misconception.
A frameshift mutation occurs when one or more base pairs are inserted or deleted in a gene, disrupting the normal sequence of nucleotides and altering the genetic code.
The embryos of terrestrial vertebrates are protected from desiccation and injury by being encased in a fluid secreted by the amnion, a membrane that surrounds the developing fetus.
Inositol triphosphate (IP3) is a second messenger that stimulates the release of calcium ions into the cytoplasm.
To synthesize an RNA/DNA hybrid from a single-stranded RNA template, you need a primer (either DNA or RNA) and reverse transcriptase.

The Hardy-Weinberg law requires that a population of organisms meet certain conditions to maintain genetic equilibrium. One exception to this is the exchange of genes with other populations, which disrupts the equilibrium.
The Barr body is a region of heterochromatin found in the nuclei of female mammalian cells, which is a type of densely packed, inactive DNA.
The correct answer is respiration, as respiration is a process that removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, not adds to it.

The concept of punctuated equilibrium suggests that species evolve rapidly and then remain unchanged for a long time, with periods of rapid speciation (bursts) followed by long periods of stability (unchanging lineages).
When an influenza virus enters a cell, it immediately starts to replicate its genetic material and synthesize viral proteins.
Spiral cleavage refers to the phenomenon where early cell divisions in an embryo occur at an oblique angle to the polar axis, resulting in cleavage symmetry.
Targeting of a newly synthesized protein to a destination other than cytosol or plasma membrane is most likely to require two different signal peptides.

In Sweden, red fox populations are limited by hares, but are also affected by the mange mite parasite. As mite populations increase, fox populations will decline, while hare populations will increase, as there are no other major predators at the site besides foxes.
The cell nucleus contains DNA (I) and RNA (III), but not just protein (II).

Archaea, Eukarya, and Bacteria are the three major domains of life. Archaea and Eukarya use the transcription factors TBP and TFIIB, while Bacteria does not. This suggests that Archaea and Eukarya diverged after their common ancestor diverged from Bacteria.
In sea urchin oocytes, a rise in intracellular free calcium triggers the release of proteolytic enzymes that prevent polyspermy.
Mycorrhizal fungi provide a benefit to many plants by increasing their ability to absorb water and nutrients from the soil.

Experiments on song development in birds show that a young male reared in isolation, exposed only to a different bird species song, will develop a song repertoire without typical characteristics of his own species. This suggests that a birds song is both instinctive and learned.
A retrotransposon is a type of mobile genetic element that moves from one location in the genome to another through a reverse transcription process, not by replicating itself.
The biomes with the highest rate of leaching and cycling of nutrients are tropical rainforests, where nutrient-rich soil is constantly being broken down and replenished.
Enzymes are effective in facilitating chemical reactions because they lower the activation energy required for the reaction to occur, thereby speeding up the conversion of reactants to products.

The point where natality (birth rate) and mortality (death rate) rates are equal is known as zero population growth. This occurs when the number of births and deaths in a population are balanced, resulting in no net change in the population size.
The wings of a bat and a butterfly are analogous structures, meaning they share a common function (flight) but have different forms and evolutionary histories.
The cell type that makes up the pith tissue at the center of a dicot stem is parenchyma.
Transposons are mobile DNA elements that can insert themselves into an existing genome.
Primary succession is the process of pioneer species colonizing a bare substrate, such as rock, sand, or glacial till, marking the beginning of ecosystem development.

Brood parasites like cuckoos deceive host birds into raising their young by mimicking the begging calls of the hosts own offspring. The host birds instinct to respond to these cues allows them to efficiently feed their own young, and the genes that enable this deception remain in the population.
Cell motility in a cultured fibroblast includes all of the following EXCEPT clathrin.

Hamiltons rule states that an altruistic trait can evolve if the fitness benefit to the recipient (b) is greater than the fitness cost to the donor (c) multiplied by the coefficient of relatedness (r).
Plants adapt to hot environments by developing features that minimize water loss.
The text describes connective tissue, listing several components that can be found within it, with the exception of collagens, fibroblasts, and collagen.
The correct answer is Y chromosome.

A bird species nests in treetops instead of cliff ledges because a more aggressive bird species occupies the cliff ledges. The treetop-nesting birds are occupying their natural and realistic habitat niche.
R-selected species are typically characterized as having a high reproductive rate, rapid growth rate, and early maturity, but NOT high competitive ability.
A DNA strand with the sequence 5CGA TTG 3 has a complementary sequence of 5GCA ACA 3.
Ferns undergo a life cycle called alternation of generations, where a dominant sporophyte (spore-producing stage) alternates with an independent gametophyte (gamete-producing stage).
In a striated muscle (skeletal muscle), the correct statement is that tropomyosin blocks the myosin binding site on actin in the relaxed state, preventing muscle contraction.

Aggressive ants live in a tropical trees thorns and feed on oil-rich bodies produced by the tree. To test the hypothesis that ants defend the plant by killing or chasing away leaf-feeding insects, the best experiment would be to remove the oil-rich bodies and observe the ants behavior.
The sight organs of crustaceans and insects contain ommatidia, which are the individual visual units of the compound eye.

An embryologist studying the development of a vertebrate organism from zygote to fetus would conclude that the embryo shares common features with other vertebrates, such as fish and birds, during its development.

The larvae of a stem-boring beetle emerge from eggs in the center of a 5-year-old wood twig and eat their way out. As they move towards the outside, they encounter the following tissues and tissue regions in order: phloem, cambium, xylem, and then the bark.
The pairs of cellular components that can be separated by low-speed centrifugation are the nucleus and cytoplasm, and the mitochondria and ribosomes.
Increasing the total surface area available for diffusion would increase the rate at which a gas diffuses between the alveoli of the lung and the blood within a pulmonary capillary.
The structures responsible for gas exchange in a woody stem are called lenticels.
The correct answer is not among the options, which are aposematic coloration, chemical defenses, and masting synchronous fruiting.
Introns are NOT excised from the primary transcript before it gains a 5 cap and a 3 polyA tail.
A healthy person sitting at rest begins to breathe rapidly, which leads to a decrease in partial pressure of carbon dioxide and a decrease in concentration of hydrogen ions in the blood.
The correct anatomical order of structures in the mammalian female reproductive tract is: Oviduct (Fallopian tube) -> Uterus -> Cervix -> Vagina.
A marine ecosystem region characterized by intense sunlight and nutrient-rich waters is not the pelagic zone.

Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is a hereditary disorder that prevents the repair of ultraviolet damage to DNA in humans. As a result, individuals with XP are more likely to accumulate thymine dimers, a specific type of molecular lesion, in their DNA.
Chemosynthetic bacteria can produce their own food without sunlight because they obtain energy by oxidizing inorganic substances like ammonia, sulfur, or hydrogen.
The text lists several options that can serve as intracellular messengers, but acetylcholine is the exception.
The correct statement that is incorrect is shoot apical meristem formation occurs after seed formation.
Mouse sperm bind to a glycoprotein (ZP3) in the zona pellucida of eggs, triggering the acrosomal reaction. Injecting eggs with antibodies that bind to ZP3 would NOT block in vitro fertilization.
Random mating does not promote linkage disequilibrium.

In an experiment, the gray crescent was intentionally placed in only one of the two blastomeres resulting from the first cleavage of an amphibian zygote. The two blastomeres were then separated. The expected outcome is that the blastomere containing the gray crescent will develop into a complete but smaller embryo.

Nerve outgrowth from a developing neuron starts at the growth cone at the axon tip, where microspikes extend and retract to move the cone forward. Exposure to cytochalasin B during this stage causes the microtubules in the axon to undergo reversible dissociation.
Monoclonal antisera contain antibodies from a single B lymphocyte, while polyclonal antisera contain antibodies from multiple B lymphocytes.
The first groups of animals to develop lung tissue capable of supporting their respiratory needs without additional gas exchange organs were not insects, mammals, or amphibians.
A species with the ability for long-distance dispersal is most likely to become cosmopolitan in distribution, meaning it can spread to and thrive in many different parts of the world.
In the formation of the earliest cells, the component that most likely arose first is the cell membrane, followed by the cytoplasm and ribosomes, and finally the nucleus.
Prior to 1859, it was already established that fossilized remains of extinct species exist.
Fungi participate in decomposition, symbiotic relationships, and the production of antibiotics, but NOT association with humans to produce ringworm or fermentation to produce alcohol.
A protein is synthesized in the cytoplasm and must cross the chloroplast membrane to reach its destination in the thylakoid lumen.

During the mammalian cardiac cycle, blood is transferred from the venous side to the arterial side, but this transfer does not result in an equal increase in venous pressure and decrease in arterial pressure.
The Golgi apparatus in a eukaryote is oriented in the cytoplasm with its cis face closest to the endoplasmic reticulum.
In a monocot plant, water enters the plant at the roots through the cytoplasm of cells, not through the Casparian strip or pericycle.
The correct answer is not stomatal guard cell, which is a type of plant cell that does not undergo programmed cell death to become functional.
Angiosperms are distinguished from gymnosperms by having seeds enclosed in ovaries.

The text describes a goose species that nests on cliffs and beaches, and its chicks must make their way to the ocean after hatching. Many cliff-nesting chicks die from falling, but cliff nesting may still be adaptive because it confers a higher fitness than beach nesting.
Immunoglobulins with epsilon heavy chains, found on the surface of mast cells and basophilic leukocytes, are classified as IgE antibodies.
A fluorescent molecule of 1,000 daltons enters an adjacent cell by passing through a gap junction, allowing for direct communication and exchange of materials between cells.
Annelids and arthropods are similar in that they belong to different phyla, but share some common characteristics.
The human genome encodes proteins for approximately 2% of its total content.
Air has a higher O2 concentration compared to water.
Organisms in the kingdom Protista are eukaryotic, meaning their cells have a true nucleus.
The kinetochore is the section of a chromosome that attaches to the mitotic spindle during cell division.
The plants growth along the trellis is not due to phototropism (growth towards light).
If an enzymes activity remains constant across a wide pH range, it suggests that both ionizing groups on the enzyme and substrate are involved in the reaction, rather than just one or the other.
In a cross between a tall violet plant (DDWw) and a dwarf white plant, the expected phenotypic ratio of the progeny is 1 tall violet and 1 tall white.
Cancer cells, like normal cells, need a surface to attach to in order to grow in culture.
Techniques to demonstrate protein binding to specific DNA sequences include Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and Electrophoretic Mobility Shift Assay (EMSA).
Adequate serum levels of calcium are maintained in humans by the secretion of parathyroid hormone.
The amino acid ornithine is regenerated during the urea cycle, similar to how oxaloacetate is regenerated during the citric acid cycle.
Angiosperms, a type of flowering plant, have a unique characteristic called double fertilization, which is not found in other plant groups.
Mammals are homeostatic for all aspects except blood pH, which is not a homeostatic variable.
The crouching of very young birds in response to a predators shape overhead is an example of a fixed action pattern.
In primates, species with high sexual dimorphism (visible differences between males and females) often have intense competition among males for mates.
In an actively photosynthesizing plant, the palisade mesophyll tissue would have the highest rate of oxygen production.

A theory suggests that pollen grains exposure to water during thunderstorms releases starch granules, which are small enough to trigger asthma attacks. The starch granules are released due to osmotic shock caused by the sudden change in osmotic pressure between the pollen grains interior and the surrounding environment.

Hybrids between plants with different chromosome numbers are often sterile, but if their chromosome number doubles, their descendants can regain the ability to reproduce sexually because their chromosomes can pair normally.
Phalloidin is a toxin that binds to actin subunits and disrupts actin function. It most directly affects microfilaments, which are a type of cytoskeleton structure composed of actin subunits.
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes that a population is not experiencing gene flow, mutation, and genetic drift, but does not assume random mating or absence of selection.
The statement some are photosynthetic is NOT true about fungi.
The src oncogene encodes an enzyme called tyrosine kinase, which adds phosphate groups to specific cellular proteins.

C4 and CAM plants both reduce photorespiration, but they use different strategies. C4 plants fix CO2 in mesophyll cells and perform the Calvin cycle in bundle sheath cells, while CAM plants fix CO2 and perform the Calvin cycle in mesophyll cells.
The correct sequence of membranes in a chloroplast, from innermost to outermost, is: thylakoid membrane, inner membrane, outer membrane.
Antibiotics that affect bacterial cells do not interfere with DNA synthesis, protein synthesis, or peptidoglycan synthesis.
In Drosophila silvarentis, polytene chromosomes are observed under a light microscope, but they are not formed through repeated DNA replication followed by nuclear division.
Colchicine is the agent that induces polyploidy in a dividing eukaryote.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts are both found in plant cells, but chloroplasts are also found in some protists, such as algae and certain protists.
Cyanobacteria are distinct from green unicellular algae because they lack a nucleus.
The stabilization of the alpha helix structure in a protein is primarily attributed to factors other than hydrogen bonding between peptide backbone atoms.
The target of digestion of a nucleosome dimer to nucleosome monomers by DNase is the linker DNA.
A thermophilic and methanogenic prokaryote with isoprenylglycerol ethers in its membrane is likely an archaeon.

High relative humidity is the exception, as it actually slows down transpiration from plants, while the other options (temperature, light, wind, and water availability) increase the rate of transpiration.
None of the options are true. The text appears to be a trick question, and all the options are incorrect statements.
In eukaryotic photosynthetic cells, when electrons flow cyclically through the electron transport chain associated with photosystem I, ATP is synthesized.
Marine birds maintain their internal osmolarity by producing dilute urine in their kidneys, but this is not the correct answer.

A small rodent species eats seeds from only one type of pine and typically has a litter size of 2-3, which is unusual for small rodents. This suggests that the rodents exhibit high parental investment, meaning they invest a lot of time and resources in their young.
The greatest contributor to the dry mass of organic matter in an oak tree is the trees own photosynthesis, which converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen through photosynthesis.
For evolution to have occurred, the frequencies of some alleles (different forms of a gene) in a populations gene pool must have changed over successive generations.
According to evolutionary theory, a trait is considered optimal if it provides the best return for the cost compared to alternative forms of the trait, leading it to prevail over other forms.
The rate of reduction of acetaldehyde to ethanol by alcohol dehydrogenase increases with increasing acetaldehyde concentration, reaching a maximum rate after which further increases have no effect.

Mutations in DNA can result in the expression of a new phenotype when the altered genetic information is translated into a different amino acid sequence, leading to a change in the structure or function of a protein. This can occur through various mechanisms, such as changes in the genetic code, altered splicing patterns, or changes in gene regulation.
A competitive inhibitor does not compete with the substrate molecule for the same enzyme binding site, but rather binds to a different site, preventing the enzyme from binding to the substrate.

The brains ability to detect differences in stimulus intensity is not related to the amplitude of the action potential, but rather to the variation in another factor that changes with stimulus intensity.

Net primary productivity in terrestrial ecosystems tends to increase towards the tropics because warm temperatures and abundant water in the tropics enhance photosynthesis, allowing for increased plant growth.

Proteins on mouse and human cells surfaces were observed moving together in a plane on a fused cell membrane. This was achieved by producing a heterokaryon, a cell culture technique that combines the nuclei of two cells from different species into a single cell.
Gene flow between populations leads to an increase in genetic homogeneity in the metapopulation.
A nucleosome is a subunit of DNA and protein consisting of 134-base-pair long stretches of DNA wrapped around a protein octamer.
In a temperate ecosystem, photoperiod (day length) is the most dependable environmental signal for a plant to initiate flowering at the correct time of the year.

Mitochondria produce ATP in a low-pH environment. The correct explanation for this effect is not related to increased acid concentration in the mitochondria matrix or increased oxygen concentration causing proton pumping to the intermembrane space.
The text states that an organism belonging to the nekton is a whale.

A fixed action pattern is a behavioral response in animals that is innate, meaning it is present from birth, and is not learned through experience. It is a pre-programmed response to a specific stimulus, and is not influenced by the animals previous experiences.
The adaptation that would limit pollination by bees and promote hummingbird pollination is NOT patterns of ultraviolet color on the petals.
In flowering plants, double fertilization occurs when one sperm fuses with the egg to form a zygote and another sperm fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm.
Mutation of homeotic cluster genes in Drosophila typically leads to developmental defects in the identity of specific body parts, resulting in altered body patterning and morphology.
Root pressure in plants causes water to enter the roots through osmosis.

Cholesterol is taken into cells through the internalization of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol complexes. The process involves several steps, but NOT endosome formation or receptor-mediated endocytosis.
The two main types of xylem cells that provide support and transport water and minerals in plants are tracheids and vessel elements.

Mimicry is a strategy that helps organisms adapt to their environment. Batesian mimicry is a type of mimicry where a harmless species evolves to resemble a harmful or distasteful species to avoid predators.
Keystone species have a significant impact on ecosystems because they prevent superior competitors from driving inferior species to extinction.

Geneticists use mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) to study the relatedness of animal populations because it is passed from mother to child and does not undergo recombination, making it a reliable indicator of maternal lineage.
When humans alter an ecosystem, it tends to become simpler and less diverse, disrupting natural population regulation. This leads to the presence of large populations of a limited number of species.

A female fruit fly with gray body and normal wings mates with a male with black body and vestigial wings, resulting in offspring with gray bodies and vestigial wings. This outcome cannot be explained by the segregation of alleles.
The largest active pool of carbon on Earth and the one that contributes the most to carbon cycling is not the atmosphere, but rather the oceans.
Charles Darwins proposed conditions for natural selection do not include competition for limited resources, overproduction of offspring, or differential survival and reproductive success.
The cohesion-tension theory states that the evaporation of water from leaf mesophyll cells generates tension in the water column, which pulls water up the xylem.
Fungis cell walls are reinforced by chitin, a key component that provides structural support and protection.
Proton pumps play a role in loading sugars into the phloem for transport in plants. This process requires ATP.

An early-successional plant community is characterized by high ratios of primary production to standing crop biomass, meaning that the rate of plant growth and production is high compared to the amount of biomass present.
The symplastic pathway for the movement of sucrose from mesophyll cells to the phloem is not through companion cells, phloem parenchyma, or fibers, but rather through sieve tube cells.
The most direct cause of polyteny in somatic cells of certain organisms is endoreduplication.
The correct answer is indeed the ends of actin filaments move closer together.
Short-term changes in plant growth rate are thought to be caused by increased extensibility of cell walls in response to the plant hormone auxin.
RNA is believed to have played a crucial role in the evolution of life due to its ability to self-replicate (II) and occur in great quantities on early Earth (I).
The organism described has a lobed thallus, rhizoids, and gemmae, and it is not a fern or a moss.

The kin selection theory proposes that an organisms altruistic behavior in social groups is driven by the desire to protect its genetic relatives. When a bird sounds an alarm call to alert others to a predator, it may be motivated by the fact that the call benefits its relatives who share its genes, even if it puts the bird itself at risk. This theory suggests that altruism can evolve because it increases the survival and reproductive success of the birds genetic kin.
The plant with the characteristics mentioned (swimming sperm, tracheids, separate gametophyte and sporophyte phases, and no seeds) is most closely related to ferns.
An oligotrophic lake is characterized by clear water, low nutrient levels, and a limited amount of algae growth.
Sea urchins are more closely related to frogs than snails because they share a common embryological feature with chordates, specifically the development of the mouth pore after the anus pore.
Elastin is not a globular protein found in connective tissue.
In a cloning experiment on Xenopus laevis frogs, tadpole intestinal cells were transplanted into zygotes with removed nuclei, resulting in a small percentage of normal frogs.
The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma of chloroplasts in plant cells.
Chiasmata are visual evidence of genetic recombination during meiosis, which is the process by which gametes (sperm or egg cells) are formed.
Gondwana and Laurasia were formed first during the separation of the elements of Pangaea through continental drift.
Prokaryotes and eukaryotes share the trait of bidirectional replication, meaning that their DNA is replicated in both directions from a single starting point.
